newsitem.title: UK: BA's long-range B-777s hit "teething problem".
newsitem.headline: BA's long-range B-777s hit "teething problem".

text.p: British Airways Plc said on Friday that it expects to put its new Boeing 777 twinjet aircraft back on transatlantic service within the next 10 days after solving a "teething problem" with the engines.

The airline said it had moved the three aircraft off long range operations over water onto European and Middle Eastern routes at the beginning of March after engineers suspected there had been excessive wear in some gearbox bearings in the General Electric GE-90 engines. "We took a decision to withdraw them from transatlantic routes as a precaution because of some teething problems," a spokesman said. "A solution for this has been identified by our engineers and is being implemented to have them back in extended range operation within the next 10 days."

The GE-90 powered version of the world's largest twinjet airliner has been plagued by controversy in Britain ever since BA chose GE engines in preference to domestically-made Rolls-Royce Trents for its prestigious launch order for 777s.
In 1995 there were concerns over the turbofan blades after a failed bird-strike test, which delayed the first 777 deleiveries under BA's initial order for 15 aircraft.
